look_here_first: Look for alternate, hairy and often glandular leaves; frequently subclasping upper leaves; branching yellow ray-and-disk flower heads. Inspect side of heads for glandular phyllaries and the coarse hairs at their tips; scent alone is unreliable.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Aromatic, branching, taprooted annual or biennial; stem sparsely to densely spreading-hairy and glandular.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Alternate, lower leaves often petiolate and upper leaves sessile and sometimes partly clasping; variable ovate to lanceolate, toothed or nearly entire; check multiple mid and upper leaves.

key_traits.label: Heads
key_traits.text: Yellow ligulate ray florets and yellow tubular disk florets; side-view involucre with glandular and hairy phyllaries.

key_traits.label: Subspecies
key_traits.text: FNA separates subsp. subaxillaris by a terminal tuft of coarse hairs on outer/mid phyllaries (often 6–28) versus subsp. latifolia without distinct tuft (occasionally 1–2 hairs); geography and season matter.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Ray and disk cypselae can differ; macro/microscopic examination for final polish.

lookalikes.differences: Pluchea camphorata has non-yellow rayless pinkish/purplish heads; within Heterotheca verify upper leaf bases, vestiture, phyllaries and reproductive structures rather than flower color alone. Other Heterotheca comparison pending matched photo review.
